newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products stable as extra supply heads east.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products stable as extra supply heads east.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were stable on Tuesday, despite weaker crude prices, with supplies flowing out of the region to the Far East.
Gas oil looked marginally softer with more Russian material heard offered and the arb opportunity eastwards less attractive.
"Mideast gasoil has fallen so while the arb still works out of the Med, there is less intensity," said one trader.
Some traders said Russians were offered out of the Black Sea at fob high quotes flat to +$1 for second half material.
Non Russian 0.2 percent gas oil was heard offered at fob high quotes +$3-3.50, but nothing was heard done.
A diesel cargo was sold at cif high EN590 quotes -50 cents cif France.

Gasoline was slightly lower in line with weaker crude prices but traders said the market was fairly balanced in terms of supply and demand with spring refinery maintenance in the region cancelling out the effects of fairly slack demand.

The naphtha situation was looking slightly less tight with supply out of Tunisia, Greece and Turkey making up for a squeeze on cargoes out of key suppliers such as Egypt and Algeria after strong demand from the East drained supply.
End users assessed naphtha cargoes at $1-$1.5 above quotes.
Fuel oil values steadied in the Med area with high sulphur cargoes supported by news some 140,000 tonnes of material was headed to the Far East to profit from higher prices.
One vessel took 60,000 tonnes of Turkish material, the second 80,000 tonnes of high sulphur bought from an Italian refiner last Friday at fob high quotes +75 cents.
Low sulphur cargo prices remained notionally around the $103/106 level with cheap transatlantic supplies being offered. Buyers heard firm offers at the $106 level with room for negotiation down.
